description: The launcher's Mods page against a mods folder, through its Qt Test driver (test_launcher_mods, offscreen, a fresh home folder with the game folder the setup makes): the rows and their lines, a switch, the order (Move down, a drag's drop), Remove with its confirmation, a dropped mod folder, a dropped Mod Crate folder handed to the import library, an import without a disc. The expected lines are frozen here AND recomputed from each mod.json by the judge (the rules of  'Mods').

usa_mod.why: a mod folder made over the North American disc (base.region NTSC-U) dropped on this European game folder (the PAL disc used for development), with the archive recipe an import writes (CRASH6/CRASH.BD ranges recording the North American archive it was made over: its size and hashes from a real USA crate's import, no game data; the folder's recipe is a few zeros): the badge NTSC-U; the summary says the disc it was made for; first in the warning colour 'Left out on this disc: made for the North American disc.' -- the game's base check leaves it out on this disc, and the game's own Mods page no longer says so; the warning names the Crate Mod Loader settings it asks for, the notes are the crate's '!' lines. A mod of whole files made for the other region is composed by the game all the same: the summary's region alone, no left-out line (test_launcher_mods: beta)

replace.text: The copy you have is removed first.
replace.folder_declined: Nothing was added: you keep Copied mod 1.
replace.folder_accepted: Copied mod replaced the copy you had; its switch and its place in the order are kept. It takes effect the next time the game starts.
replace.crate_declined: Nothing was added: you keep Cave Remix 2.0.
replace.crate_accepted: Cave Remix replaced the copy you had; its switch and its place in the order are kept. It takes effect the next time the game starts.
replace.why: ONE RULE for an id the mods folder has: the page asks first for the drop of a ready mod folder and for an import (Add a mod..., a drop); declined, nothing changes; accepted, the new copy replaces the old one (staged, then swapped) and keeps its switch and its place in the order
